name: Nanai
catalog_quote: Таким образом, наиболее подверженными редукции оказываются гласные под ударением, поскольку последнее всегда в нанайских словах падает на конечный слог. [Thus the vowels most subject to reduction turn out to be the vowels under stress, since the latter always falls, in Nanai words, on the final syllable.]
sweep_summary: Nanai (nana1257, catalog fixed-strict final, deciding quote = incidental p. 37 remark in Avrorin 1959). The single sweep item, Baitchura 1979 (ZAS 13: 281-308), is the only instrumental study of Nanai word prosody and is relevant, but no open copy exists (HathiTrust search-only, Google Books snippet view, not on archive.org/DiVA/MENAdoc); Snippets pulled from the Google Books volume show Baitchura's conclusion that Nanai is the exception among Manchu-Tungus languages: in disyllables the FIRST vowel has the higher mean tone (+1.2 tones on average, dansa 'book' 0 t. to hoda 'value' +2 t.), while the SECOND vowel carries the rising tone movement - instrumental support for the Sunik-style split (initial level prominence, final rise) that Avrorin explicitly left open, so it refines rather than overturns the final coding (priority high to obtain; library print only). Side finds via the same snippet route: Oskolskaya 2020 (Oxford Guide) confirms non-distinctive final stress in Najkhin Nanai as a pitch accent with final lengthening and notes the Gorin dialect de-emphasises the last syllable; Kazama 2023 (Routledge) says 'the primary expiratory stress falls on the initial syllable... though there may be a raised pitch on a later syllable', which contradicts a dynamic-final reading (priority high, paywalled DOI 10.4324/9781315728391-14). Two open Baitchura articles in Orientalia Suecana (27-28: 108-117; 38-39) were fetched sources from Wayback copies of DiVA and read: both are Udehe only (their 'Nanai' hits are the Udehe word nani), silent on Nanai; their footnotes name Baitchura's Russian Manchu-Tungus stress reports (Leningrad 1969/1971, Leeds 1975, Tomsk 1976) as further targets. Hölzl 2018 (open, fetched sources) quotes Baitchura 1979: 294 on Nanai question intonation only. Best first-hand statement read: Avrorin 1959: 62-63, the dedicated stress section ('всегда падает на последний слог слова, независимо от его морфологической структуры', with suffix-chain examples), which should replace the p. 37 vowel-reduction remark as the deciding locator, with a caution that the prominence is chiefly tonal and that dynamic stress may be initial (Sunik 1958; Kazama 2023; Baitchura's first-vowel tone level).

new_statements.quote: По месту в слове нанайское ударение является строго регулярным, связанным — оно всегда падает на последний слог слова, независимо от его морфологической структуры. Оно оказывается на последнем слоге не только тогда, когда слово включает в свой состав ряд суффиксов, но даже и тогда, когда в состав слова включается одна, а иногда и две-три суффиксальные частицы. Например: [хото́н] 'город', [хотонка́н] 'горожане', [хотонканду́] 'горожанах', [хотонкама́т] 'подобно горожанам', [хотонкамада́] 'даже подобно горожанам'.
new_statements.translation: As to its place in the word, Nanai stress is strictly regular, bound: it always falls on the last syllable of the word, regardless of its morphological structure. It ends up on the last syllable not only when the word contains a series of suffixes but even when one, sometimes two or three suffixal particles are included in the word. E.g. xotón 'town', xotonkán 'townspeople', xotonkandú 'in townspeople (loc.)', xotonkamát 'like townspeople', xotonkamadá 'even like townspeople'.
new_statements.citation: Avrorin, V. A. 1959. Grammatika nanajskogo jazyka, t. 1. Moskva-Leningrad: Izd. AN SSSR, section 'Udarenie', pp. 62-63.
new_statements.locator: pp. 62-63 ('Ударение'); p. 62 for the placement sentence, p. 63 for the secondary-stress and Sunik passages
new_statements.reading: Fixed final stress on the whole word including suffixal particles (catalog 'fixed-strict' final is supported). Avrorin adds three cautions that the record should carry: (1) the prominence is mixed musical-dynamic, mainly a tone rise with very slight intensity and no effect on quantity; (2) a possible weak secondary dynamic stress on the stem-final syllable (participles: on the tense suffix), pending instrumental check; (3) Sunik's dissent - weak dynamic stress on the FIRST syllable plus a tone rise on the last - which Avrorin leaves for instrumental verification. This sweep's snippet evidence bears exactly on that dispute: Baitchura's 1968-69 instrumental data (ZAS 13, 1979) show the first vowel with the higher mean tone and the final vowel with the rising contour, and Kazama 2023 states primary expiratory stress on the initial syllable with raised pitch later, while Oskolskaya 2020 keeps final pitch-accent stress (Najkhin) with Gorin-dialect variation. The coding 'final' stands for the tonal/culminative prominence described by Avrorin and Oskolskaya, but the record should note that dynamic prominence may be initial (Sunik 1958, Kazama 2023, Baitchura's first-vowel tone level).

audit.reasoning: Quote check: both Avrorin 1959 sentences (pp. 23, 37) are verbatim in the held Russian scanned at the stated pages, and p. 37 was re-verified against the held djvu by fresh scanned. The classification (fixed-strict final) rests on the standard Academy reference grammar, which we hold in full, and is corroborated by held Avrorin 1968 §4 and not contradicted by the held IL RAS minlang sketch (which calls dynamic stress non-contrastive and notes phrase-driven final lengthening). Weakness is presentational, not evidential: the record's top-level quote/cite/loc/grade are empty and the deciding citation points at an incidental remark in the vowel-reduction section instead of the dedicated stress section pp. 62-63 ('строго регулярным, связанным — оно всегда падает на последний слог слова, независимо от его морфологической структуры', with suffix-chain examples). Recommended: move the deciding locator t

sources.quote: По своему характеру нанайское ударение может быть определено скорее всего как смешанное — музыкально-силовое. Основной его особенностью является некоторое повышение тона ударного гласного [...] По месту в слове нанайское ударение является строго регулярным, связанным — оно всегда падает на последний слог слова, независимо от его морфологической структуры. [...] О. П. Суник замечает, что в нанайском слове всегда имеется два ударения: слабое силовое ударение, падающее на первый слог, и тоническое ударение (повышение тона), падающее на последний слог. Инструментальная проверка должна помочь окончательному разрешению этого спорного вопроса.
sources.note: [In character Nanai stress is best defined as mixed, musical-dynamic; its main feature is a certain raising of the tone of the stressed vowel... As to its place in the word Nanai stress is strictly regular, bound: it always falls on the last syllable of the word regardless of its morphological structure... Sunik notes that a Nanai word always has two stresses: a weak dynamic stress on the first syllable and a tonic stress (tone rise) on the last. Instrumental verification must help settle this disputed question.] Fixed final stress, mainly tonal, slight intensity, no effect on quantity; possi…

sources.quote: In general questions, the tone movement in the vowel of the final syllable has a clearly and strongly manifested rising character, whereas the mean and the maximal tone heights surpass those of the preceding vowels in cases in which no interrogative particle is present in the sentence. If there is such a particle (e.g., nu), the rise of the tone at the end of the sentence is not so high, its pitch being a little lower in comparison to the tone heights of vowels at the beginning of the sentence.
sources.note: Second-hand quotation of Baitchura 1979 on Nanai question intonation only (final-syllable tone rise as interrogative cue); nothing on word-stress placement.
